frequency_question: How often do bilateral state treaties with fixed expiration dates successfully complete the intergovernmental drafting, review, and signing process before expiration, given full administrative cooperation?
membership_rule: Includes all bilateral treaties involving sovereign states that reached an expiration date with an expressed intent to renew; excludes treaties where renewal was abandoned due to lack of interest or unilateral withdrawal.

cases.name: US-Russia Plutonium Management and Disposition Agreement amendment
US-Russia Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START I) short-term extensions
Columbia River Treaty operational review extensions

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named; selective sample of high-stakes bilateral resource/security agreements.
known_gaps: Limited to prominent publicly documented state-to-state agreements.
skeleton: Cases of bilateral treaties facing imminent expiration where technical committees required sequential drafting (60 days), legal review (30 days), and ministerial execution (30 days).
multiplier: 5 observed completed renewals divided by 5 attempted renewals under compressed timelines
validity_reason: Intergovernmental bureaucratic procedures for treaty drafting and signing change slowly over decades.
